With f_i at the bin centre, as the hardware read it, the bound is 328.1 m/s: the half bin, f' in eq. 59

statement: df down to 1 kHz to measure 500 m/s

statement: RMS phase error below 4 deg above 20 dB (Fig. 3)
note: Poole's closed form (eq. 82) gives 4.056 deg at 20 dB: '4 deg above 20 dB' is that value rounded, and the Monte Carlo agrees with eq. 82; 2000 trials per SNR through the chain's window, Gaussian noise

statement: V* rms error 0.56 m/s for a 4 deg phase error, T = 0.5 s, f = 5.9 MHz
note: cells at 23.1 dB each, so the phase difference has 4 deg rms; with 20 dB per cell, as paper 2's sentence reads, the difference has sqrt(2) x 4.05 deg and V* 0.798 m/s

statement: Echo criterion: at most the 16 highest spectral values per cell over an amplitude criterion, from a 1024-sample FFT
measured: same threshold (9.8 dB over mean): P_fa 7.5e-05 (known mean) vs 8.9e-05 (P2); Pd at 10 dB 0.58 vs 0.57; a 40-bin spread echo keeps 16 vs 39 bins
note: the cap of 16 never binds on noise; it truncates spread and multiple echoes, which the P2 detector keeps for the tracker.  The P2 detector estimates the mean from the cell (ordered statistic), so it pays a small CFAR loss against the known-mean criterion

statement: Group velocity V' = V* + f dV*/df from a swept ionogram; the indirect estimate within 20 % of the direct dR'/dt
note: a parabolic layer whose shape changes so that V' at 6.4 MHz is constant (30 dB per cell); paper 2's V* -8.68 m/s and dV*/df -5.60e-6 m/s/Hz are of the same order; the 9 soundings nearest 6.4 MHz fitted with a parabola
